title: Ajisai MCP result
description: One envelope for every Ajisai MCP tool result. `status` separates the three outcomes the boundary keeps distinct: a successful run (which includes a reason-carrying NIL), an Ajisai language error carrying its diagnosis, and a failure of the host rather than of the program. An optional field carrying no value is omitted rather than sent as `null`, so `diagnosis`, `aiDiagnostic`, `message` and `contractDecls` are simply absent from a plain success — test for presence, not for `null`. The text content block of a tool result carries this same object serialized, so a text-only client receives the whole result and not a summary of it.

stackElided.description: Present on an `error` whose failing stack was too large to send in full. An error report's answer is its diagnosis; the stack is residual state, so the values of the slots that do not fit a byte budget are dropped and this record says which. Absent whenever nothing was dropped, which is every success and every ordinary error. A successful result is never elided: it *is* its stack, and an oversized one is reported as `responseTooLarge` instead.

slots.description: One entry per dropped slot, in stack order.

index.description: Position in `stack` and `stackDisplay`. Slots keep their index: a dropped slot is replaced in place, never removed, so a diagnosis that points at stack depth still points at the same thing.

approxBytes.description: Roughly what the slot would have serialized to, counted without building the text.

elements.description: Direct children, for a collection. Absent for a leaf.

partiality.description: The registry's derivation over the Words the body calls: `projecting` when one can answer a reasoned NIL of its own, `partial` when one can raise on operands of the right kind, `total` otherwise.

suggested.description: A paste-ready `#:contract` line for this Word, written in the keys and values of this same object, so pasting it back verifies exactly what was reported.

contracts.description: Inferred contracts for the user-defined Words in the submitted source (`infer_contracts` only). Every key a registered Word's contract also has (`word_contract`, and `CONTRACT` inside the language) is spelled the same and takes the same values, so an inferred and a registered contract compare directly. Reports each cost axis as its class alone; exactness is observable through `suggested`, which names only the axes the declaration checker can verify.

runtimeMetrics.description: How the runtime went about its work: which cache answered, which fast path fired, how often a plan was rebuilt. Optimizer observations, not budgets — read `resourceUsage` for what a ceiling would judge. `executionSteps` appears in both and carries the same reading; it is kept here for compatibility and belongs in `resourceUsage`.

resourceUsage.description: What this run spent of the budgets that could have refused it. Every key names a key of `mcp.limits` and carries the same number the ceiling compared against — read from the counter the check reads, not a parallel copy — so an agent can subtract one from the other and know what it has left. Only the accumulating ceilings appear: `bigintBits` and `algebraicTerms` are checked per result and never accumulated, so there is no peak to report and none is invented.

numericWork.description: Internal arithmetic work charged, in limb-multiply units, against the `numericWork` ceiling.

collectionWork.description: Element operations charged inside collection Words — copies, order comparisons and equality probes — against the `collectionWork` ceiling. Priced from the operand, so an element that is wide, nested or algebraic costs more than a machine word; a collection Word loops inside one execution step, so this is the only counter that can see it.

registrySchemaVersion.description: Schema version of the packaged Word registry (`word_contract` only). Distinct from the envelope's own `schemaVersion`.

matches.description: Canonical registry entries matching the requested Word or alias (`word_contract` only).

suggestions.description: Registry names closest to an unmatched request, best match first (`word_contract` only). Empty whenever `matches` is non-empty.

serverVersion.description: Version of this MCP adapter — a separate component from the Ajisai engine below it. A stored result names both, so a missing field can be told apart from a field this adapter version never sent.

backend.description: Which of the two interchangeable backends answered. They are semantically equivalent — `backend/parity-test.js` asserts it case by case — so this identifies the execution path for auditing, not a difference in meaning.

limits.description: The host profile applied to this call. Every entry is pinned by a case in `golden/limits.json`.

hostError.description: A failure of the host, never of the Ajisai program. `code` is the stable identifier to branch on; `message` is safe to show a model and deliberately carries no host paths, environment-variable names or spawn detail.

limit.description: The declared `mcp.limits` entry this failure is about, when it is about one.

debugCheck.description: One repair step. Match on `code`; `title` and `detail` are display text and may be reworded or gain locales.

resourceLimitFacts.description: Which declared ceiling a resource-limit failure crossed, or a generative Word declined a result under (the diagnosis of a NIL(spaceExhausted), which can name `materializedElements`). `resource` names an entry of `mcp.limits`. `observed` is what crossed it — a real measured size for the size ceilings, but for a cumulative work ceiling only the budget spent at the moment of refusal, which sits a hair over `limit` however far over the request was. Where that is so, `progress` carries the number to act on instead.

progress.description: How far an operation charged as it goes had got when its budget ran out. Present only where `observed` cannot say how much smaller the input must be; absent for every ceiling whose `observed` is a real size. `completed` is the answer rather than a hint at it: the budget bought exactly that many units of this data, so retrying with that many is what fits.

candidates.description: Known Words closest to an unrecognized name, best match first. Empty for every other cause class.

wordContract.description: One canonical entry of the generated `spec/words.json` registry, reproduced verbatim.

cost.description: What the Word charges on each of the three metered resources the runtime counts (`executionSteps` / `numericWork` / `collectionWork`). The classes join pointwise under concatenation, so a phrase's bound on an axis is the widest class any of its Words declares there — which is what lets a caller budget a program without running it.

exactTerm.description: One term c·√m of the normal form: the rational coefficient numerator/denominator and the square-free radicand m (1 for the rational term).

protocolNode.description: One stack value as observed at the host boundary. Every field is derived from the value itself, never from the Word that produced it (LANG.VALUES.DENOTATION). A vector's own elements are observedValue nodes in turn (see `value` below), so this definition is recursive.

type.description: The value's domain (LANG.VALUES.DISJOINT), discriminating `value`'s shape. A NIL is `nil` wherever it stands, including in truth position, where it reads as UNKNOWN (LANG.VALUES.TRUTH).

value.description: Shape depends on `type`: nil -> null; boolean -> boolean; number -> {numerator, denominator} (arbitrary-precision decimal strings, the denominator positive); string or symbol -> string (a symbol's bare name); vector -> an array of observedValue; record -> {keys, values}, two arrays of observedValue of equal length, aligned position by position (LANG.RECORDS.STRUCTURE). null for any type when `elided` is present.

costAxis.description: A sound upper bound on one metered resource. `class` bounds how the charge grows with the Word's input; `exact` records that some contribution provably attains it, rather than the bound being a safe over-approximation.

protocolSemantics.description: Present on every node except an interior (rank >= 2) tensor node. Every field is optional. Both host surfaces emit the same set, because both render it with one function (rust/src/agent/report.rs::semantics_json).

truthValue.description: Present on a Boolean node, and only there (rust/src/types/value_absence.rs::truth_value). UNKNOWN is a NIL (LANG.VALUES.TRUTH) and is observed through `absence`, not here.

approximate.description: true when the node is an irrational scalar (LANG.VALUES.EXACT), whose `value` is therefore a rational approximation: the best convergent the observation budget affords, or, for a value too large to afford even one, a term-by-term one. `exactTerms` is the value. Never present otherwise.

exactTerms.description: An irrational scalar's exact multiquadratic normal form, structured for computation: one term per {numerator, denominator, radicand}. The stack display writes the same terms as one token (`sqrt(2)`, `1/1+sqrt(2)`).

protocolAbsence.description: Present only on a nil-type node. `reason` is the stable, machine-readable identifier LANG.VALUES.NIL calls the entire observable content of a NIL (one of spec/outcomes.json's NIL reasons); it is absent only for a NIL an implementation could not yet label. `detail` is the text a `userDeclared` reason carries, which is part of that reason. `origin` and `recoverability` are diagnostic state beyond the reason, informational only: a program cannot observe them, and two NILs with one reason are one value whatever their origin. `diagnosis` nests the structured diagnosis object docs/dev/agent-cli-output-contract.md describes, when the runtime produced one.

protocolElided.description: Present only in the stack of a CLI/MCP error report, on a slot whose value was dropped to keep the report deliverable (rust/src/agent/error_stack.rs). `type` and `semantics` still describe what the value was (less an algebraic value's `exactTerms`, whose count moves here); `value` is null. Tell it apart from a genuine NIL by `type`, which names the real domain, and by this field's presence.
